evidence: Cic. Sen. 38: ita sēnsim sine sēnsū aetās senēscit
terms.comment: From sentiō: so slowly that one hardly notices; the opposite of repente (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.14.7: pedetentim et gradātim (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: ita sēnsim sine sēnsū aetās senēscit nec subitō frangitur, sed diūturnitāte exstinguitur
phrases.english: so life grows old little by little, without our noticing, and does not snap suddenly but goes out with long time

phrases.latin: farīnam in mortārium inditō, aquae paulātim additō subigitōque pulchrē
phrases.english: put the flour in the bowl, add water little by little, and knead it well

sources: Lewis & Short: paulatim · Lewis & Short: sensim · Lewis & Short: gradatim
